title: Enlarging two bounded subcomplexes to a common pair that kills a derived-tensor kernel and catches an image, inside a cardinal bound

standard_prerequisites.name: Arithmetic of cardinals: the maximum of a finite family of cardinals bounds the cardinality of a union or of a finite product of sets of those cardinalities
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: invoked at proof lines 29924-29932, where kappa = max(|A|, |B|, aleph_0) is fixed and the statement is announced to be used without further mention
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the size estimate for the smallest subcomplexes generated by finitely many elements, for the free resolution of B, and finally for the index set of the two sums that define M_2 and N_2, which is what makes property (3) true.

standard_prerequisites.name: Every module admits a resolution by free modules of bounded cardinality, and the derived tensor product is computed by the total complex of the tensor product with such a resolution
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: recorded at proof lines 29962-29965 as a resolution ... -> F^{-1} -> F^0 -> B by free A-modules F_i with |F_i| at most kappa, with the cohomology of M_1 tensor B computed by Tot(M_1 tensor F)
standard_prerequisites.use: Turns the abstract derived tensor product into an explicit complex of cardinality at most max(kappa, |M_1|), which is the estimate used for the cohomology of the small subcomplexes.

standard_prerequisites.name: Derived tensor product commutes with filtered colimits, so a cohomology class that dies after tensoring with B already dies after tensoring with a small enough subcomplex
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: used at proof lines 29955-29959, where M and N are exhibited as filtered colimits of the small subcomplexes, and at proof lines 29975-29978
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the finite collections E_xi and F_xi for a kernel class xi, and the analogous collections E_eta and F_eta for an image class eta, inside the small colimit system.

standard_prerequisites.name: The hypothesis that a : M -> N induces an isomorphism M tensor^L_A B -> N in D(B) is an isomorphism on cohomology, and it factors through the map to N_1
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: used at proof lines 29972-29974 for the kernel class xi and at proof lines 29981-29983 for the image class eta
standard_prerequisites.use: Identifies the target of the vanishing condition for xi and the source of the preimage for eta with objects living in the N_1 and M_1 systems, which is what lets the enlargement be driven by finitely many elements.

core_obligations: Fix kappa = max(|A|, |B|, aleph_0), adopt the notation |M| = |union M^i| for a complex, and rewrite the bound of property (3) as max(kappa, |M_1|, |N_1|); declare that the arithmetic of cardinals used from here on is applied without further mention (proof lines 29924-29932).

Construct the supply of small subcomplexes: for every pair of collections E = {E^i}, F = {F^i} of finite subsets of M^i and N^i, take the smallest subcomplexes M_1(E,F) and N_1(E,F) containing the given subcomplexes and the chosen finite sets and compatible under a, and check the two size estimates |M_1(E,F)| at most max(kappa, |M_1|) and |N_1(E,F)| at most max(kappa, |N_1|), together with the fact that M and N are the termwise filtered colimits of these systems (proof lines 29935-29959).

Bound the cohomology of a small tensor product: produce a resolution of B by free A-modules F_i with |F_i| at most kappa, note that the cohomology of M_1 tensor^L_A B is computed by Tot(M_1 tensor F), and conclude |H^i(M_1 tensor^L_A B)| at most max(kappa, |M_1|) (proof lines 29962-29967).

Handle a kernel class: for an element xi of H^i(M_1 tensor^L_A B) that maps to zero in H^i(N_1), use the hypothesis on a to see that xi dies in H^i(N) and then in H^i(M tensor^L_A B), and apply the filtered-colimit compatibility of the derived tensor product to find finite collections E_xi, F_xi with xi already zero in H^i(M_1(E_xi,F_xi) tensor^L_A B) (proof lines 29970-29978).

Handle an image class: for an element eta of H^i(N_1), use the hypothesis on a to see that the image of eta in H^i(N) lies in the image of H^i(M tensor^L_A B), and again find finite collections E_eta, F_eta such that eta maps into H^i(N_1(E_eta,F_eta)) inside the image of H^i(M_1(E_eta,F_eta) tensor^L_A B) (proof lines 29980-29988).

Close by summation: define M_2 as the sum of all M_1(E_xi,F_xi) and M_1(E_eta,F_eta) and N_2 as the sum of all N_1(E_xi,F_xi) and N_1(E_eta,F_eta), inside M and N respectively; the construction gives properties (1) and (2) by the two preceding paragraphs, and property (3) follows because the index set of the sums has cardinality at most max(kappa, |M_1|, |N_1|) (proof lines 29990-30009).
proof_roadmap: Fix the cardinal kappa = max(|A|, |B|, aleph_0) and set up the size bookkeeping, replacing the bound in property (3) by max(kappa, |M_1|, |N_1|) (proof lines 29924-29932).

Build the filtered system of small subcomplexes M_1(E,F), N_1(E,F) generated by finite collections of elements with the two size estimates, and record M and N as its filtered colimit (proof lines 29935-29959).
Estimate the cohomology of a small subcomplex by resolving B through free A-modules of size at most kappa (proof lines 29962-29967).

For every kernel class xi and every image class eta select the finite collections that already realize its vanishing or its preimage inside the small system, then sum the corresponding small subcomplexes to obtain M_2 and N_2 and verify the three properties, the last one by the cardinality of the index set (proof lines 29970-30009).
difficulty_reason: The lemma concerns an arbitrary ring map A -> B, complexes M of A-modules and N of B-modules, a map a : M -> N that becomes an isomorphism after the derived tensor product with B, and given subcomplexes M_1, N_1 compatible under a; the conclusion produces enlarged subcomplexes M_2, N_2 with an explicit cardinal bound max(kappa, |M_1 union N_1|) that kills one kernel and catches one image in every cohomological degree (statement lines 29894-29921). The proof is not a routine diagram chase: it first has to build a filtered system of small subcomplexes generated by finitely many elements, with a size estimate, then estimate the cohomology of the derived tensor product through a free resolution of B of cardinality at most kappa, and finally use that the derived tensor product commutes with the filtered colimit to realize each individual obstruction in a single small stage (proof lines 29935-29988). The closing step is a cardinality count over the index set of the two sums that define M_2 and N_2, so the bound in property (3) is genuinely proved rather than assumed (proof lines 29990-30009). Every input is inside the counted span except the standard facts about cardinals, free resolutions and filtered colimits that are named in the editorial notes; the author marks two sub-steps as having details omitted, both of which are routine and none of which is load-bearing for the main line.
